1	# 0001. Multi-country content differentiation strategy
2	
3	Status: Accepted
4	
5	## Context and problem statement
6	
7	The same Angular build must sell car insurance in Colombia and Chile. Form fields, their
8	validations and copy, the available plans, and the terms & conditions text all differ by
9	country, and the non-technical business team must be able to change all of that from
10	Strapi without requesting a deployment. We need a content-modeling strategy in Strapi —
11	and a corresponding consumption pattern in Angular — that differentiates content by
12	country without duplicating the application or the Strapi schema per country.
13	
14	## Decision drivers
15	
16	- Single app, single build, single Strapi schema serving both countries (explicit scope
17	  rule in the test).
18	- Non-technical business team edits fields/plans/terms per country with no code change.
19	- Colombia and Chile share the same language (Spanish) but differ in regulation, identity
20	  document, vehicle identifier, currency and copy — the variation is **business/regulatory**,
21	  not linguistic.
22	- Must stay easy to extend to a third country later without a schema migration.
23	- No write-enabled token may reach the browser; the front end only ever reads.
24	
25	## Considered options
26	
27	1. **Explicit `country` field on each content-type**, consumed by Angular via a REST
28	   filter (`filters[country][$eq]=CO`). One schema for `form-field`, `plan`,
29	   `terms-and-condition`, each entry tagged with its country.
30	2. **Strapi i18n plugin, using locale as a proxy for country** (e.g. `es-CO`, `es-CL`),
31	   relying on Strapi's built-in locale negotiation and localized entries.
32	3. **Separate content-types per country** (e.g. `form-field-co`, `form-field-cl`), or
33	   separate Strapi projects per country.
34	
35	### Option 1 — explicit `country` field
36	
37	- Good: country is a first-class, explicit business concept, not overloaded onto a
38	  mechanism meant for language. Adding a third country is just new entries with a new
39	  country value — no schema change, no new content-type.
40	- Good: a single `CountryContentService` in Angular can enforce the country filter on
41	  every request in one place, keeping the "same app, same build" rule trivially true.
42	- Good: keeps Strapi's i18n plugin free for its actual purpose (translating copy into
43	  another *language*, e.g. English) if that's ever needed later, without conflict.
44	- Bad: the front end is responsible for always passing the country filter; forgetting it
45	  on one query could leak cross-country content. Mitigated by routing every content read
46	  through one shared service (see "Consequences" below).
47	- Bad: no automatic locale negotiation from the browser/CDN "for free" the way i18n gives
48	  you — country selection has to be resolved explicitly (see Consequences).
49	
50	### Option 2 — i18n plugin as country proxy
51	
52	- Good: built-in Strapi feature; the admin UI already has a locale switcher and
53	  per-locale publish state.
54	- Bad: conflates two independent axes (*language* and *country/regulatory content*).
55	  Colombia and Chile both use Spanish, so there is no language difference to encode here —
56	  using locale for country is a semantic misuse that will confuse the content team (the
57	  locale switcher reads as "translate this," not "this is a different country's rules").
58	  If the business later wants an actual English version for either country, it immediately
59	  collides with this scheme.
60	- Bad: i18n relationships in Strapi are heavier to manage for content types that also need
61	  country-specific *structural* differences (e.g., a field that only exists in Chile),
62	  since i18n assumes the same shape translated, not a different shape per locale.
63	
64	### Option 3 — separate content-types or separate Strapi projects per country
65	
66	- Bad: directly violates the "single app/single schema" driver — adding a country means
67	  duplicating content-types (or whole projects), and Angular would need per-country code
68	  paths to know which content-type to call, undermining "the same build serves both
69	  countries."
70	- Bad: doubles the maintenance and review surface for every future change.
71	- Not pursued further; included only to document why it was rejected.
72	
73	## Decision outcome
74	
75	Chosen option: **Option 1 — explicit `country` field on each content-type**, because it
76	models country as what it actually is (a business/regulatory dimension), keeps a single
77	schema and a single build, and scales to a third country with zero schema changes.
78	
79	Implementation consequences for Strapi and Angular:
80	
81	- Content-types `form-field`, `plan`, `terms-and-condition` (and any future
82	  country-varying content-type) each carry a `country` enumeration field (`CO` | `CL`,
83	  extensible).
84	- Strapi Public role permissions remain `find` / `findOne` only; country filtering happens
85	  via query parameters on those same endpoints — no extra permission surface.
86	- Angular reads country-scoped content exclusively through one `CountryContentService`
87	  (built in Phase 5) that always applies the `country` filter, so no call site can
88	  accidentally omit it.
89	- For this test, the current country is resolved by an explicit, user-visible country
90	  selector persisted in the wizard's signal-based state (not geo-IP or subdomain
91	  routing) — documented as an intentional simplification in `README.md`, since automatic
92	  country resolution is out of scope for the functional requirements given.
93	
94	### Consequences
95	
96	- Good: adding Argentina or Mexico later is pure content work in Strapi, no code or
97	  schema change.
98	- Good: business team edits per-country content directly, no deployment, matching the
99	  core requirement.
100	- Good: keeps the door open for genuine i18n (translation) later without redesigning this.
101	- Bad: correctness now depends on every content read going through the shared
102	  `CountryContentService` — enforced by code review (`code-reviewer` agent + human) rather
103	  than by the framework itself.
104	- Bad: country selection in this test is manual (a selector), not automatic; acceptable
105	  for the stated scope but would need a real resolution strategy (domain, session,
106	  geolocation) before production use.
107

1	# 0002. Dynamic form rendering and reserved semantic field keys
2	
3	Status: Accepted
4	
5	## Context and problem statement
6	
7	US-01's step-1 form is fully dynamic: fields, their order, validation and copy are
8	configured per country in Strapi (`form-field` content-type, ADR-0001). The resulting
9	form value is naturally a dynamic map keyed by each field's Strapi `key`
10	(`Step1FormValue`), not a fixed TypeScript shape — the business team can add, remove or
11	reorder fields without a code change.
12	
13	Two downstream consumers, however, need specific semantic fields, not just "the form has
14	whatever the business configured":
15	
16	- US-02's simulated pricing rule needs the driver's age, the vehicle's year, and whether
17	  usage is personal or commercial.
18	- US-03's summary screen needs to render policyholder name, (masked) document, contact
19	  info, and vehicle make/model/year/identifier in a predictable layout.
20	- US-01's own legal-age and vehicle-year validators need to know *which* configured field
21	  is "date of birth" or "vehicle year," since those rules aren't plain min/max checks.
22	
23	We need a way to bridge a fully dynamic, business-configured form with code that needs
24	specific semantic fields, without hardcoding field presence/order (which would break the
25	core "business team adds/removes/reorders fields without a code change" requirement) and
26	without the business team being able to silently break pricing/summary/validation by
27	renaming a field's key.
28	
29	## Decision drivers
30	
31	- Must not reintroduce a fixed/hardcoded form shape.
32	- Must give the legal-age/vehicle-year validators (US-01), the pricing rule (US-02), and
33	  the summary screen (US-03) a reliable way to find "the date of birth field" etc. among
34	  dynamically configured fields.
35	- Must stay simple enough for the business team (editing Strapi) to follow without
36	  training.
37	- Avoid adding new Strapi schema if a naming convention achieves the same result.
38	
39	## Considered options
40	
41	1. **Reserved semantic `key` convention.** A fixed, documented set of `key` values (e.g.
42	   `fullName`, `documentNumber`, `dateOfBirth`, `vehicleYear`, `vehicleUsage`, …) that,
43	   when used as a `form-field.key` in Strapi, are understood by the front end to carry
44	   that specific meaning. The business team can still add *extra* fields with any other
45	   key; only the fields the app depends on for validation/pricing/summary must use these
46	   exact keys.
47	2. **Dedicated `semanticRole` field on `form-field`.** Add an explicit enum field in
48	   Strapi (`semanticRole: 'dateOfBirth' | 'vehicleYear' | 'vehicleUsage' | 'none'`) so the
49	   mapping is data, not a naming convention.
50	3. **No semantic bridge.** US-02/US-03 each read the raw dynamic map directly, assuming
51	   keys independently at each call site.
52	
53	### Option 1 — reserved key convention
54	
55	- Good: zero new Strapi schema; reuses the `key` field that already has to be unique and
56	  stable per field.
57	- Good: simple to document (one table in this ADR) and simple for the business team to
58	  follow — "use this exact key for this field."
59	- Bad: nothing in Strapi structurally enforces it; a business user could create a
60	  date-of-birth-equivalent field under a different key, silently breaking legal-age
61	  validation. Mitigated by seed data always including the reserved keys and a loud,
62	  explicit error if one is missing for the active country (see Consequences).
63	
64	### Option 2 — dedicated `semanticRole` field
65	
66	- Good: explicit and structurally enforced.
67	- Bad: adds schema complexity for a problem a naming convention already solves at this
68	  project's scale; every new semantic need would require a Strapi migration to extend the
69	  enum, cutting against "business team changes things without a deployment" for anything
70	  beyond the roles anticipated today.
71	
72	### Option 3 — no bridge, ad hoc per consumer
73	
74	- Bad: no single source of truth for which keys matter; US-02 and US-03 could each assume
75	  different key names for the same concept — exactly the inconsistency this ADR exists to
76	  prevent. Not pursued further.
77	
78	## Decision outcome
79	
80	Chosen option: **Option 1 — reserved semantic key convention**, because it solves the
81	problem with zero added Strapi schema, and its failure mode (a business user picking the
82	wrong key) is cheaply mitigated at the application boundary.
83	
84	**Reserved keys** (used as `form-field.key` wherever a country's form includes that
85	semantic field):
86	
87	| Reserved key | Type | Meaning | Consumed by |
88	|---|---|---|---|
89	| `fullName` | text | Policyholder full name | US-03 summary |
90	| `documentType` | select | e.g. `CC`/`CE` (CO), `RUT` (CL) | US-03 summary |
91	| `documentNumber` | text | Identity document number (masked at render time) | US-01 masking, US-03 summary |
92	| `dateOfBirth` | date | Triggers the legal-age (≥ 18) validator | US-01 validation |
93	| `email` | text | Contact email | US-03 summary |
94	| `phone` | text | Contact phone | US-03 summary |
95	| `vehicleMake` | select | Vehicle make | US-03 summary |
96	| `vehicleModel` | text | Vehicle model | US-03 summary |
97	| `vehicleYear` | number | Triggers the vehicle-year range validator | US-01 validation, US-02 pricing |
98	| `vehicleIdentifier` | text | Placa (CO) / patente (CL) | US-03 summary |
99	| `vehicleUsage` | select (`personal`\|`commercial`) | Feeds the simulated pricing rule | US-02 pricing |
100	
101	Each country's `form-field` seed data must include all of these keys (with per-country
102	labels/copy/validation), plus any extra country-specific fields under any other key.
103	
104	### Consequences
105	
106	- Good: `Step1FormValue` stays a dynamic map (`{[key]: value}`), while a typed
107	  `ReservedStep1Fields` projection (reading exactly these keys) is what US-02 and US-03
108	  actually consume — this reconciles all three specs' data contracts without hardcoding
109	  the whole form shape.
110	- Good: a country-specific extra field never breaks pricing/summary/validation, since
111	  those only ever read the reserved keys.
112	- Good: extending to a new semantic need later is a documentation change (add a row here)
113	  plus front-end code, not a Strapi migration.
114	- Bad: if seed data for a country omits a reserved key, or a business user later
115	  deletes/renames that field, the dependent feature breaks. Mitigated by: seed data for
116	  both countries always including every reserved key, and the front end surfacing a loud,
117	  explicit "missing required field: dateOfBirth" error during development/content review
118	  (not a silent fallback) when a reserved key is absent for the active country — this is a
119	  content-configuration error to fix in Strapi, not a case to design around in Angular.
120	- Bad: relies on documentation discipline rather than a compiler/schema guarantee;
121	  acceptable at this project's scale — revisit Option 2 if the number of reserved keys
122	  grows significantly.
123

1	# US-01 — Policyholder and vehicle data form
2	
3	Status: Approved
4	
5	## Story
6	
7	As a person interested in insuring my car, I want to enter my data and my vehicle's data
8	in a simple form, so that I receive insurance options suited to my country and my
9	vehicle.
10	
11	## Business rules
12	
13	- Each field is configured in Strapi with: label, type (text, number, select, date,
14	  checkbox), required flag, validations, help text, error message, order and country.
15	- Select fields (for example, make or city) get their options from Strapi.
16	- The vehicle year cannot be later than next year or more than 20 years old.
17	- The policyholder must be of legal age.
18	
19	## Acceptance criteria
20	
21	```gherkin
22	Scenario: Form configured by country
23	  Given fields are configured in Strapi for Colombia and for Chile
24	  When I open the application in the context of a country
25	  Then I see only the fields configured for that country, in the defined order
26	
27	Scenario: Field validation
28	  Given I am filling out the form
29	  When a field does not meet its configured validation
30	  Then I see the configured error message next to the field
31	  And I cannot move to the next step
32	
33	Scenario: Configuration change without deployment
34	  Given the business team adds a new published field in Strapi
35	  When I reload the application
36	  Then the new field appears without code changes
37	
38	Scenario: Keep data when going back
39	  Given I moved on to step 2
40	  When I go back to step 1
41	  Then my data is still filled in
42	```
43	
44	## Gaps and edge cases
45	
46	- **Country resolution**: per ADR-0001, the current country is read from the explicit
47	  user-visible country selector in wizard state, not geo-IP/subdomain. This spec assumes
48	  that selector already set a `country` value (`CO` | `CL`) before step 1 renders; the
49	  selector itself is out of scope for this story.
50	- **Loading state**: while `form-field` entries are being fetched from Strapi for the
51	  active country, the form area must show a loading indicator and not render a partial or
52	  empty form.
53	- **Error state**: if the Strapi request fails (network error, 5xx) or returns zero fields
54	  for the selected country, the form must show an explicit error state with a retry
55	  affordance — not a silently empty form, and not a crash.
56	- **Empty state**: zero configured fields for a country is a valid (if degenerate) Strapi
57	  state; it must be distinguished from a fetch error (see above) — e.g. "no fields
58	  configured for this country yet" vs. "couldn't load the form."
59	- **Unpublished fields**: Strapi's draft/publish workflow means a `form-field` entry can
60	  exist but be unpublished. The front end only ever reads published entries (consistent
61	  with Public role `find`/`findOne` access per CLAUDE.md) — an added-but-unpublished field
62	  must not appear until published, which is what AC "Configuration change without
63	  deployment" exercises.
64	- **Duplicate `order` values**: if two fields share the same `order` for a country, the
65	  tie-break is undefined by the story. Flagged as an open question below rather than
66	  inventing a silent tie-break rule.
67	- **`select` field with no options configured**: a `select` field whose options array is
68	  empty must not render as a broken/empty dropdown blocking the user; treated as a
69	  misconfiguration to surface, not silently skip (see Open questions — exact UX for this
70	  isn't specified).
71	- **Field types and native validation mapping**: `date` fields need a concrete min/max
72	  policy for the vehicle-year rule (see Data contract) — modeled as a `number` field
73	  semantically representing a year, not a native `<input type="date">`, since "vehicle
74	  year" is a year, not a calendar date. This is called out explicitly because the story's
75	  field type enum includes `date` generically but the one business rule mentioning a year
76	  needs a numeric range check, not a date picker.
77	- **Legal-age validation**: requires a `date` field for date of birth and a computed
78	  check (today − dob ≥ 18 years) that is *not* a simple Strapi-configured min/max, since
79	  "legal age" is a moving target relative to today's date, not a fixed bound. This is a
80	  built-in validator in the Angular form, applied whenever a field is semantically a
81	  date-of-birth field (see Open questions — how the field's semantic role, e.g. "this is
82	  the DOB field," is identified from Strapi config).
83	- **Masking sensitive identifiers**: per the project's accessibility & security
84	  checklist, the identity-document field's value must be masked in the UI (e.g. after
85	  entry/on blur), consistent with "sensitive identifiers (document numbers) are masked."
86	- **Back-navigation persistence**: "keep data when going back" implies step-1 form state
87	  must survive navigating to step 2 and back without a round-trip to Strapi or the
88	  backend — i.e., it is held in wizard-level state (signals), not re-fetched or reset on
89	  re-entering step 1. Re-entering step 1 must also not re-trigger the loading state for
90	  the field configuration (already-fetched config is reused, not re-requested with a
91	  visible spinner each time).
92	- **Validation re-check on re-entry**: if a field's value was left invalid and the user
93	  navigated away via browser back/forward (not only the wizard's own "back"), the
94	  invalid state and its error message must still be shown when step 1 is shown again.
95	- **Field reordering mid-session**: if `order` changes in Strapi between the initial load
96	  and a reload, the story only promises the *new* order "without code changes" after a
97	  reload — it does not promise live reordering without reload. No action needed beyond
98	  what AC 3 already covers.
99	- **Dynamic, typed validation**: since fields and their validators come from configuration
100	  rather than compile-time code, the step-1 form must build Angular reactive-form
101	  validators at runtime from the Strapi config while keeping the resulting form value
102	  typed (see Data contract) — no `any` in the resulting form model, per CLAUDE.md.
103	- **Keyboard and labels**: every dynamically-generated field must still get a
104	  programmatically associated `<label>`/`aria-describedby` pair and be reachable in
105	  logical tab order, including `select` and `checkbox` types, since the field set itself
106	  is only known at runtime.
107	- **Responsive layout**: the dynamically-generated field list must reflow correctly at
108	  mobile widths regardless of how many fields a given country has configured (field count
109	  is data-driven, not fixed at design time).
110	
111	## Data contract
112	
113	```ts
114	type FieldType = 'text' | 'number' | 'select' | 'date' | 'checkbox';
115	
116	type CountryCode = 'CO' | 'CL';
117	
118	interface FormFieldOption {
119	  label: string;
120	  value: string;
121	}
122	
123	interface FormFieldValidation {
124	  // Exact validation rule shapes (regex source, min/max, min/max length) are an
125	  // open question — see "Open questions". This interface models the superset of
126	  // constraints implied by the story's business rules (vehicle year range, required).
127	  min?: number;
128	  max?: number;
129	  minLength?: number;
130	  maxLength?: number;
131	  pattern?: string;
132	}
133	
134	// Strapi content-type: `form-field`
135	interface FormFieldAttributes {
136	  key: string;
137	  label: string;
138	  type: FieldType;
139	  required: boolean;
140	  validation?: FormFieldValidation;
141	  helpText?: string;
142	  errorMessage: string;
143	  order: number;
144	  country: CountryCode;
145	  options?: FormFieldOption[]; // present only when type === 'select'
146	}
147	
148	interface FormFieldEntry {
149	  id: number;
150	  attributes: FormFieldAttributes;
151	}
152	
153	// Front-end wizard state for step 1 (policyholder + vehicle data).
154	// Keyed by each field's Strapi `key`; values are typed per FieldType at the
155	// reactive-form-control level, not as a single flat `any` record.
156	type FormFieldValue = string | number | boolean | null;
157	
158	interface Step1FormValue {
159	  [fieldKey: string]: FormFieldValue;
160	}
161	
162	interface Step1State {
163	  country: CountryCode;
164	  fields: FormFieldEntry[]; // as loaded from Strapi for `country`, pre-sorted by order
165	  value: Step1FormValue;
166	  status: 'loading' | 'error' | 'empty' | 'ready';
167	}
168	```
169	
170	## Definition of done
171	
172	- [ ] Step 1 renders only the published `form-field` entries whose `country` matches the
173	      active country, sorted by `order` — nothing from the other country is visible or
174	      fetched. *(AC: Form configured by country)*
175	- [ ] Each field's configured validation runs on submit/step-advance; a failing field
176	      shows its configured `errorMessage` next to the field via `aria-describedby`, and
177	      the wizard does not advance to step 2 while any required/invalid field remains.
178	      *(AC: Field validation)*
179	- [ ] A new published field added in Strapi for the active country appears after an
180	      application reload, with no front-end code change, respecting its configured
181	      `order`. *(AC: Configuration change without deployment)*
182	- [ ] Navigating from step 1 to step 2 and back preserves every previously entered
183	      step-1 value exactly as the user left it, without a re-fetch of field
184	      configuration and without resetting validation state. *(AC: Keep data when going
185	      back)*
186	- [ ] Vehicle year field rejects a value later than next year or more than 20 years old,
187	      surfacing the configured error message.
188	- [ ] Policyholder date-of-birth field rejects an age under 18, surfacing an error
189	      message.
190	- [ ] `select` fields render their options exclusively from the Strapi-configured
191	      `options` list.
192	- [ ] The identity-document field's value is masked in the UI per the project's
193	      accessibility & security checklist.
194	- [ ] The full step-1 form (including dynamically generated fields) is completable with
195	      keyboard only, with every field programmatically labeled.
196	- [ ] Step 1 renders correctly at mobile and desktop widths.
197	- [ ] Loading, error, and empty states for the Strapi field fetch are each handled
198	      explicitly and distinguishably.
199	- [ ] No `any` appears in the step-1 form value or field-configuration types.
200	
201	## Open questions
202	
203	- Exact validation pattern/regex for Colombian identity documents (cédula de ciudadanía /
204	  cédula de extranjería), Colombian license plate (placa), Chilean RUT, and Chilean
205	  license plate (patente) are not specified in the source material. Rather than inventing
206	  precise regexes, this spec leaves `FormFieldValidation.pattern` as a free-form string
207	  sourced from Strapi config — the actual regex values are a Strapi *content* decision
208	  for whoever configures the fields, not a front-end hardcoded rule. Needs confirmation
209	  from the business/test owner on whether these patterns should ship as seed data (and if
210	  so, what the exact patterns are) or remain fully business-team-authored.
211	- How is a field's *semantic role* (e.g. "this field is the policyholder's date of
212	  birth," "this field is the vehicle year") identified from Strapi config for rules that
213	  aren't plain min/max (legal age relative to today, vehicle-year window relative to the
214	  current year)? Options include a reserved `key` naming convention (e.g. `key ===
215	  'dateOfBirth'`) or a dedicated semantic-role field in the content-type. Needs a decision
216	  before the Strapi `form-field` schema is finalized (likely as a follow-up ADR or a
217	  decision captured directly in the `strapi-architect` agent's schema work).
218	- Tie-break behavior when two fields for the same country share the same `order` value is
219	  unspecified — stable-by-insertion-order, by `id`, or treated as a content error to
220	  surface to the business team? Needs a decision before implementation.
221	- UX for a misconfigured `select` field (type `select` with an empty `options` array):
222	  render nothing, render disabled, or surface a visible configuration-error state? Not
223	  specified by the story.
224	- Is the identity-document masking format (which characters are shown vs. masked, and
225	  when unmasking is allowed, e.g. on focus) specified anywhere, or is any reasonable
226	  masking acceptable for this story?
227	
228	## Resolutions (approved 2026-11-21)
229	
230	- **Validation patterns**: remain free-form `pattern` strings authored as Strapi content
231	  (not hardcoded in Angular). `strapi-architect` provides reasonable example seed
232	  patterns for CO (cédula, placa) and CL (RUT, patente) as a starting point for the
233	  business team.
234	- **Semantic role identification**: resolved via a reserved `key` naming convention — see
235	  [ADR-0002](../docs/adr/0002-dynamic-form-rendering.md). `dateOfBirth` and `vehicleYear`
236	  are the reserved keys the legal-age and vehicle-year validators look for.
237	- **Duplicate `order` tie-break**: ascending `id`, applied consistently with US-02.
238	- **Empty `select` UX**: render a visible configuration-error state for that field (e.g.
239	  "this field is misconfigured — contact the business team"), never a silently
240	  broken/empty dropdown.
241	- **Document masking format**: first 2 and last 2 characters visible, the rest replaced
242	  with `•`, country formatting reapplied around the mask — same algorithm as US-03's,
243	  applied here wherever the document number is shown outside the active edit field.

1	# US-02 — Plan list
2	
3	Status: Approved
4	
5	## Story
6	
7	As a person getting a quote, I want to see the plans available for my country with their
8	price and coverages, so that I can choose the one that best fits my needs.
9	
10	### Context
11	
12	Plans, coverages, benefits and prices change by country and are managed by the business
13	team from Strapi. The business team wants to highlight one plan as "recommended" and
14	control the order in which plans appear.
15	
16	## Business rules
17	
18	- Each plan is configured in Strapi with: name, short description, base price, currency,
19	  coverages, benefits, order, recommended flag, active status and country.
20	- Only published and active plans for the country are shown.
21	- The price is shown in the country's currency and format (Colombian pesos or Chilean
22	  pesos).
23	- The final price may be adjusted by a simulated rule based on the step 1 data. The rule is
24	  documented.
25	- Only one plan can be selected.
26	
27	## Acceptance criteria
28	
29	```gherkin
30	Scenario: Plans for the country
31	  Given I completed the step 1 form
32	  When I reach the plans step
33	  Then I see only the active and published plans for my country, in the configured order
34	
35	Scenario: Recommended plan
36	  Given a plan is marked as recommended in Strapi
37	  When I view the plan list
38	  Then that plan is visually distinguished from the others
39	
40	Scenario: Plan selection
41	  Given I am on the plan list
42	  When I select a plan
43	  Then it is marked as chosen
44	  And I can move on to the summary
45	
46	Scenario: No plans available
47	  Given there are no active plans for my country
48	  When I reach the plans step
49	  Then I see a message explaining that no plans are available
50	```
51	
52	## Gaps and edge cases
53	
54	- **Loading state.** While the `plan` collection is being fetched, the plans step shows an
55	  explicit loading indicator instead of an empty list; plan selection controls are disabled
56	  until data arrives.
57	- **Error state vs. empty state.** "No plans available" (a business/content condition —
58	  the country simply has zero active+published plans) must be visually and textually
59	  distinct from a technical failure (Strapi unreachable, non-2xx response, network error).
60	  The technical-error state offers a retry action; the empty-content state does not (there
61	  is nothing to retry — it reflects actual content state).
62	- **Copy for the empty-content message is CMS-managed, not hardcoded.** Per `CLAUDE.md`,
63	  all country-specific copy lives in Strapi. This spec does not hardcode the "no plans
64	  available" sentence in Angular; the exact copy source is an open question below.
65	- **Country filter enforcement.** The plans request goes exclusively through the
66	  `CountryContentService` (ADR-0001) so the `country` filter can never be omitted at the
67	  call site. The request additionally filters `active=true` and relies on the Public role
68	  only exposing published entries (`find`/`findOne`), so no explicit "published" filter is
69	  needed beyond what the Public role already enforces.
70	- **Ordering and ties.** Plans are sorted by the Strapi `order` field ascending. If two
71	  plans share the same `order` value, the sort falls back to ascending `id` for a stable,
72	  deterministic order (see Open questions — needs confirmation this is the desired
73	  tie-break rather than a content-validation rule that forbids duplicate `order` values).
74	- **Multiple "recommended" plans.** Strapi does not enforce uniqueness on the `recommended`
75	  boolean. If the business team marks more than one plan as recommended, Angular renders
76	  the badge on every plan flagged `recommended` — it does not silently pick one. This is
77	  treated as a content-governance concern, not a front-end bug (see Open questions).
78	- **Currency formatting differs CO vs. CL.** Both Colombian pesos (COP) and Chilean pesos
79	  (CLP) are conventionally displayed with zero decimal places and a thousands separator
80	  (e.g. `$ 1.250.000`), but grouping separators and symbol placement follow each locale's
81	  convention (`es-CO` vs. `es-CL`). Formatting uses `Intl.NumberFormat` with the locale
82	  derived from the plan's `country`, not from the browser locale, so the amount always
83	  renders in the country's own convention regardless of the viewer's device settings.
84	- **Coverages/benefits can be empty.** If a plan's `coverages` or `benefits` array is
85	  empty, the corresponding section is omitted rather than rendered as an empty list or
86	  placeholder text.
87	- **Selection is exclusive.** Selecting a plan deselects any previously selected plan in
88	  the same step (single-select, radio-group semantics), per "Only one plan can be
89	  selected."
90	- **Back-navigation from the summary (step 3) to the plans step.** On returning to the
91	  plans step, the list of active+published plans for the country is re-fetched (content
92	  may have changed since the user last viewed it). The previous selection is preserved only
93	  if that same plan `id` is still present in the freshly fetched, active+published list;
94	  otherwise the selection is cleared and the user must choose again before advancing — the
95	  UI does not silently auto-select a different plan on the user's behalf.
96	- **Back-navigation from the plans step to step 1.** If the user changes step-1 answers
97	  that feed the simulated pricing rule (see Data contract) and returns to the plans step,
98	  every plan's displayed price is recomputed from the (possibly) new step-1 data; the base
99	  prices themselves are unchanged, only the simulated adjustment is reapplied.
100	- **Accessibility.** Each plan is a keyboard-operable selectable control (reachable by Tab,
101	  selectable with Enter/Space, visible focus indicator), consistent with `CLAUDE.md`. The
102	  "recommended" distinction is conveyed through more than color/an icon alone (e.g. a
103	  visually-rendered "Recommended" label plus a programmatic cue such as `aria-label` or
104	  visually-hidden text), so it is not lost to screen-reader users or color-blind users.
105	- **Responsive layout.** Plan cards stack in a single column on narrow viewports; price,
106	  "recommended" badge and the selection control all remain visible and legible without
107	  horizontal scrolling.
108	- **No pagination assumed.** The spec assumes the number of active plans per country is
109	  small enough to render in a single, unpaginated list. If the business team configures a
110	  large number of plans, pagination/virtualization is out of scope for this story
111	  (flagged, not solved, here).
112	
113	## Data contract
114	
115	```ts
116	type CountryCode = 'CO' | 'CL';
117	type Currency = 'COP' | 'CLP';
118	
119	// --- Strapi `plan` content-type ---
120	
121	interface PlanCoverage {
122	  name: string;
123	  description: string;
124	}
125	
126	interface PlanBenefit {
127	  name: string;
128	  description: string;
129	}
130	
131	interface StrapiPlanAttributes {
132	  name: string;
133	  shortDescription: string;
134	  /** Integer amount in the plan's currency, no decimals (e.g. 1250000 = COP 1,250,000). */
135	  basePrice: number;
136	  currency: Currency;
137	  coverages: PlanCoverage[];
138	  benefits: PlanBenefit[];
139	  order: number;
140	  recommended: boolean;
141	  active: boolean;
142	  country: CountryCode;
143	}
144	
145	interface StrapiEntity<T> {
146	  id: number;
147	  attributes: T;
148	}
149	
150	interface StrapiCollectionResponse<T> {
151	  data: StrapiEntity<T>[];
152	  meta: {
153	    pagination: { page: number; pageSize: number; pageCount: number; total: number };
154	  };
155	}
156	
157	type PlanListResponse = StrapiCollectionResponse<StrapiPlanAttributes>;
158	
159	// --- Front-end view model (post simulated pricing adjustment) ---
160	
161	interface PlanViewModel {
162	  id: number;
163	  name: string;
164	  shortDescription: string;
165	  basePrice: number;
166	  adjustedPrice: number;
167	  currency: Currency;
168	  coverages: PlanCoverage[];
169	  benefits: PlanBenefit[];
170	  order: number;
171	  recommended: boolean;
172	  selected: boolean;
173	}
174	
175	// --- Simulated pricing rule (see Open questions — formula is a proposed assumption) ---
176	
177	/**
178	 * Provisional shape. Field names/types must be reconciled against US-01's approved data
179	 * contract for the step-1 form once that spec is final — see Open questions.
180	 */
181	interface Step1QuoteData {
182	  country: CountryCode;
183	  driverAge: number;
184	  vehicleYear: number;
185	  vehicleUsage: 'personal' | 'commercial';
186	}
187	
188	interface PricingRuleInput {
189	  basePrice: number;
190	  step1: Step1QuoteData;
191	}
192	
193	interface PricingRuleFactor {
194	  label: string;
195	  multiplier: number;
196	}
197	
198	interface PricingRuleOutput {
199	  adjustedPrice: number;
200	  appliedFactors: PricingRuleFactor[];
201	}
202	```
203	
204	## Definition of done
205	
206	- [ ] The plans step requests plans through `CountryContentService` only, filtered by the
207	      current country and `active=true`, sorted by `order` ascending (tie-break: `id`
208	      ascending) — covers *Plans for the country*.
209	- [ ] Each plan renders name, short description, coverages, benefits, and the price in the
210	      country's currency and format, computed from `basePrice` adjusted by the documented
211	      simulated pricing rule — covers *Plans for the country*.
212	- [ ] A plan with `recommended: true` is visually distinguished (and the distinction is
213	      conveyed to assistive technology, not color/icon alone) — covers *Recommended plan*.
214	- [ ] Selecting a plan marks it as chosen (single-select) and enables navigation to the
215	      summary step; selecting a different plan replaces the previous selection — covers
216	      *Plan selection*.
217	- [ ] When the country has zero active+published plans, a CMS-sourced explanatory message
218	      is shown instead of an empty list, distinct from the technical-error state — covers
219	      *No plans available*.
220	- [ ] Loading and technical-error states are handled explicitly and are visually distinct
221	      from the "no plans available" content state.
222	- [ ] Returning to the plans step from the summary re-fetches plans and re-validates the
223	      prior selection, clearing it if the previously selected plan is no longer
224	      active/published.
225	- [ ] The whole plans step is operable by keyboard only, with visible focus and no keyboard
226	      traps.
227	- [ ] The plans step layout is responsive (single-column stacking on narrow viewports, no
228	      horizontal scroll).
229	- [ ] All Strapi-sourced data is typed against the interfaces in Data contract — no `any`.
230	
231	## Open questions
232	
233	- **Simulated pricing rule formula (needs approval).** The story requires the final price
234	  to be "adjusted by a simulated rule based on the step 1 data" and that "the rule is
235	  documented," but does not specify the formula. Proposed simulated rule
236	  (`SIMULATED-PRICING-RULE-v1`), to apply in order on top of `basePrice`:
237	  1. Driver age factor: `driverAge < 25` → ×1.15; `25 ≤ driverAge ≤ 60` → ×1.00;
238	     `driverAge > 60` → ×1.05.
239	  2. Vehicle age factor: `(current year − vehicleYear) > 10` → ×1.10; otherwise ×1.00.
240	  3. Usage factor: `vehicleUsage === 'commercial'` → ×1.20; `'personal'` → ×1.00.
241	  4. Round the result to the nearest whole currency unit (COP/CLP have no minor unit in
242	     common display).
243	  This is explicitly a **simulated, illustrative rule** (per `CLAUDE.md`: "price
244	  calculation may be simulated"), not an actuarial rating engine. It is flagged here as an
245	  assumption requiring human approval before implementation, not a silently-adopted
246	  default.
247	- **Where does the "no plans available" copy live in Strapi?** No existing content-type
248	  covers generic wizard/UI copy (the current catalogue is `form-field`, `plan`,
249	  `terms-and-condition`). Options: (a) add a field to the `plan` country scope itself is
250	  not applicable since there's no plan to attach it to when the list is empty; (b)
251	  introduce a new country-scoped singleton content-type for wizard copy (e.g.
252	  `wizard-copy`) following the same `country` field pattern as ADR-0001. Introducing a new
253	  content-type touches the content strategy, so this needs a decision from
254	  `strapi-architect` (and, per `CLAUDE.md`'s human-in-the-loop checkpoints, likely a short
255	  ADR amendment or at least explicit sign-off) before implementation.
256	- **Step-1 data contract dependency.** `Step1QuoteData` above is provisional. Its field
257	  names, types, and even which fields exist must be reconciled against US-01's approved
258	  spec and data contract once that spec is finalized, since US-02's pricing rule consumes
259	  that data directly.
260	- **Tie-break rule for equal `order` values.** This spec proposes falling back to ascending
261	  `id`. An alternative is to treat duplicate `order` values as invalid content and have the
262	  business team fix it in Strapi rather than defining front-end tie-break behavior at all.
263	  Needs confirmation.
264	- **Multiple plans marked `recommended`.** Confirm the proposed behavior (render the badge
265	  on all of them, no front-end dedup) is acceptable, or whether Strapi-side validation
266	  should constrain this to at most one plan per country.
267	
268	## Resolutions (approved 2026-11-21)
269	
270	- **Simulated pricing rule**: `SIMULATED-PRICING-RULE-v1` accepted as proposed, unchanged.
271	- **"No plans available" copy**: hardcoded, static English copy in Angular — not
272	  Strapi-configurable. Rationale: it's an edge-case message, not core business content;
273	  the test's configurability requirement targets form fields, plans and terms
274	  specifically. No new `wizard-copy` content-type is introduced, keeping the Strapi schema
275	  scoped to ADR-0001's three content-types.
276	- **Tie-break for duplicate `order`**: ascending `id`, consistent with US-01.
277	- **Multiple `recommended` plans**: render the badge on every flagged plan; no front-end
278	  dedup, no new Strapi-side uniqueness constraint.
279	- **`Step1QuoteData` reconciliation**: resolved via
280	  [ADR-0002](../docs/adr/0002-dynamic-form-rendering.md)'s reserved-key convention —
281	  `driverAge` is derived from the `dateOfBirth` reserved field, `vehicleYear` and
282	  `vehicleUsage` are read directly from their reserved keys in US-01's `Step1FormValue`.
283

1	# US-03 — Summary and payment
2	
3	Status: Approved
4	
5	## Story
6	
7	As a person who chose a plan, I want to review a summary of my quote and pay, so that I
8	become insured.
9	
10	### Context
11	
12	Before paying, the person must confirm their data and accept the terms and conditions,
13	whose text varies by country and is managed by the business team from Strapi. Payment is
14	simulated for this test.
15	
16	## Business rules
17	
18	- The summary shows the policyholder's data, the vehicle's data and the chosen plan with
19	  its final price.
20	- The document number is shown partially masked.
21	- From the summary the person can go back to edit their data or change the plan.
22	- The pay button is enabled only after accepting the terms and conditions.
23	- The payment cannot be submitted twice.
24	- On successful payment, a confirmation with a simulated quote number is shown.
25	
26	## Acceptance criteria
27	
28	```gherkin
29	Scenario: Complete summary
30	  Given I chose a plan
31	  When I reach the summary
32	  Then I see my data, my vehicle's data and the chosen plan with its final price
33	
34	Scenario: Terms by country
35	  Given I am on the summary
36	  When I view the terms and conditions
37	  Then the text matches the one configured in Strapi for my country
38	  And the pay button is disabled until I accept them
39	
40	Scenario: Successful payment
41	  Given I accepted the terms
42	  When I click pay
43	  Then the button is locked while the payment is processed
44	  And I see the confirmation with the quote number
45	
46	Scenario: Rejected payment
47	  Given the simulated payment fails
48	  When I click pay
49	  Then I see a clear error message
50	  And I can try again without losing my information
51	```
52	
53	## Gaps and edge cases
54	
55	- **Document number masking (assumption, needs confirmation).** The story requires the
56	  document number to be "partially masked" but doesn't specify the pattern. Colombia's
57	  document number (cédula) is a plain digit string; Chile's RUT includes formatting
58	  (`12.345.678-9`). Proposed rule, to be applied uniformly regardless of country:
59	  - Take the raw identifier value as entered (ignoring separators for the purpose of
60	    counting).
61	  - Keep the first 2 characters and the last 2 characters visible.
62	  - Replace every character in between with `•`.
63	  - Re-apply the country's own display formatting (dots/dash for `CL`) around the masked
64	    result, so a RUT still reads as grouped, e.g. `12.•••.•••-9`, and a CO cédula reads as
65	    `10••••••32`.
66	  - If the raw value is 4 characters or fewer, mask everything except the last character
67	    only (avoids a fully-unmasked short number).
68	  This is flagged as an assumption — see Open questions.
69	- **Simulated payment failure condition (assumption, needs confirmation).** The story says
70	  "the simulated payment fails" without saying when. Proposed simulated approach, clearly
71	  labeled as a test-only mock (never a real gateway):
72	  - The mock payment step exposes a deterministic, user-visible toggle in the UI itself
73	    (e.g. a dev/test control, or a specific fictitious card number convention such as
74	    "card ending in 0000 always fails") rather than a hidden random chance, so the
75	    rejected-payment E2E scenario is reproducible and not flaky.
76	  - A fixed, small random-failure chance is explicitly rejected for the default path
77	    because it would make `test-writer`'s E2E "rejected payment" scenario non-deterministic.
78	  This is an assumption pending confirmation — see Open questions.
79	- **Double-submit prevention.** The pay action transitions a `payment.status` signal
80	  `idle → submitting` synchronously on click; the pay button is disabled (not just
81	  visually, but via the `disabled` attribute so it's also unreachable by keyboard/Enter)
82	  for the whole `submitting` state. A second click, a second Enter keypress, or a
83	  double-tap while `submitting` is a no-op. On `rejected`, status returns to `idle` so the
84	  person can retry; on `approved`, the button stays disabled/hidden (payment is final).
85	- **Quote number format (assumption, needs confirmation).** Proposed simulated format:
86	  `<country>-<yyyy><sequence or random 6 digits>`, e.g. `CO-2026384012`, generated entirely
87	  client-side (no backend) since persistence is simulated for this test. Flagged as an
88	  assumption — see Open questions.
89	- **Back-navigation preserves data.** Going back to edit policyholder/vehicle data (US-01)
90	  or to change the plan (US-02) must not clear any previously entered wizard state. Coming
91	  back to the summary afterward must re-render it from the preserved state, re-fetch the
92	  current country's terms and conditions, and reset `termsAccepted` to `false` only if the
93	  country changed (otherwise previously accepted terms for the same country/version stay
94	  accepted — see Open questions on whether re-acceptance should always be forced).
95	- **Loading / error / empty states for terms and conditions.** The terms content comes
96	  from Strapi (`terms-and-condition`, country-scoped per ADR-0001). The summary must
97	  handle: terms loading (pay button stays disabled while loading, spinner or skeleton
98	  shown), fetch error / Strapi unreachable (visible error message, a retry action, pay
99	  button stays disabled since terms can't be shown), and the case where no terms entry
100	  exists for the current country (same error handling — never silently accept with no
101	  content shown).
102	- **Offline / payment-network failure vs. simulated rejection.** The simulated payment
103	  failure (business scenario) is distinct from a genuine client-side error (e.g. the mock
104	  payment handler throwing). Both must surface a clear, user-facing error message per the
105	  "Rejected payment" scenario, but a genuine error should be logged distinctly (e.g. to the
106	  console) for debugging, without exposing technical detail to the user.
107	- **Session persistence / refresh mid-wizard.** Per the front-end-only persistence
108	  constraint, all wizard state (policyholder, vehicle, plan, terms acceptance, payment
109	  status/result) is kept in a signal-based store backed by `sessionStorage`, so a page
110	  refresh on the summary step restores the in-progress quote instead of losing it. Closing
111	  the tab (session end) is expected to lose the data — this is in scope as "front-end-only
112	  persistence", not durable storage.
113	- **Successful payment: wizard state afterward.** After an approved payment, the person is
114	  on a confirmation screen with the quote number. The "pay button is enabled only after
115	  accepting terms" and double-submit rules imply the summary form itself should no longer
116	  be editable/re-submittable from that point; navigating back should not resurrect a
117	  payable summary for an already-approved quote. Exact behavior (locked summary vs.
118	  redirect vs. new-quote reset) is an open question.
119	- **Accessibility.** The terms-and-conditions checkbox has a programmatically associated
120	  label and its own `aria-describedby` if paired with helper/error text; the pay button's
121	  `disabled` state is reflected to assistive tech (native `disabled`, not just a CSS
122	  class); the "submitting" state is announced (e.g. `aria-live` region) so screen-reader
123	  users know the click registered; on both approval and rejection, focus moves to the
124	  resulting message (confirmation panel or error alert) so it's immediately read out; the
125	  whole flow (checkbox, back links, pay button, retry action) is reachable and operable by
126	  keyboard alone, in a logical tab order.
127	- **Responsive layout.** Summary sections (policyholder, vehicle, plan/price, terms,
128	  pay action) must reflow for narrow viewports without requiring horizontal scrolling or
129	  truncating the final price/quote number.
130	
131	## Data contract
132	
133	The policyholder and vehicle shapes are owned by US-01's spec and the plan shape by
134	US-02's; they're restated here only as the shape US-03 *consumes*, so field names must be
135	reconciled with those specs once drafted (see Open questions). The terms-and-conditions
136	and simulated-payment shapes are introduced by this spec.
137	
138	```ts
139	type CountryCode = 'CO' | 'CL';
140	
141	// Consumed from US-01's wizard state. Field names are provisional pending that spec.
142	interface PolicyholderData {
143	  fullName: string;
144	  documentType: string;   // e.g. 'CC' for CO, 'RUT' for CL — country-specific, from Strapi form-field config
145	  documentNumber: string; // raw, unmasked; masking is applied only at render time in US-03
146	  email: string;
147	  phone: string;
148	}
149	
150	// Consumed from US-01's wizard state. Field names are provisional pending that spec.
151	interface VehicleData {
152	  make: string;
153	  model: string;
154	  year: number;
155	  vehicleIdentifier: string; // country-specific label/validation, from Strapi form-field config
156	}
157	
158	// Consumed from US-02's wizard state. Field names are provisional pending that spec.
159	interface SelectedPlan {
160	  id: string;
161	  name: string;
162	  country: CountryCode;
163	  finalPrice: number;
164	  currency: string; // 'COP' | 'CLP'
165	  coverageSummary: string[];
166	}
167	
168	// Read-only Strapi content-type, country-scoped per ADR-0001, via CountryContentService.
169	interface TermsAndCondition {
170	  id: number;
171	  country: CountryCode;
172	  version: string;
173	  body: string; // rich text / markdown, rendered as-is
174	  updatedAt: string;
175	}
176	
177	// Simulated only — never sent to a real payment gateway; fictitious data only.
178	interface SimulatedPaymentRequest {
179	  quoteDraftId: string;
180	  amount: number;
181	  currency: string;
182	}
183	
184	type SimulatedPaymentResult =
185	  | { status: 'approved'; quoteNumber: string; processedAt: string }
186	  | { status: 'rejected'; reason: string };
187	
188	// Front-end wizard state for this step, signals-backed and mirrored to sessionStorage.
189	interface SummaryStepState {
190	  country: CountryCode;
191	  policyholder: PolicyholderData;
192	  vehicle: VehicleData;
193	  plan: SelectedPlan;
194	  terms: {
195	    content: TermsAndCondition | null;
196	    loading: boolean;
197	    error: string | null;
198	    accepted: boolean;
199	    acceptedVersion: string | null;
200	  };
201	  payment: {
202	    status: 'idle' | 'submitting' | 'approved' | 'rejected';
203	    result: SimulatedPaymentResult | null;
204	  };
205	}
206	```
207	
208	## Definition of done
209	
210	- [ ] Summary renders the policyholder's data, vehicle's data and chosen plan with final
211	      price (**Complete summary**).
212	- [ ] Document number is shown using the masking rule above, never in full (**Complete
213	      summary**; cross-cutting security checklist item).
214	- [ ] "Edit data" and "change plan" actions return to US-01/US-02 without losing any
215	      previously entered wizard state, and coming back restores the summary correctly.
216	- [ ] Terms and conditions are fetched from Strapi through `CountryContentService`,
217	      filtered to the current country, and the rendered text matches that country's
218	      configured entry (**Terms by country**).
219	- [ ] Terms loading/error/empty states are handled explicitly; pay button stays disabled
220	      in all of them.
221	- [ ] Pay button is disabled until the terms checkbox is checked, and the disabled state
222	      is reflected to assistive tech (**Terms by country**).
223	- [ ] Clicking pay while terms are accepted locks the button for the duration of the
224	      (simulated) processing, and a second click/Enter during that window is a no-op
225	      (**Successful payment**; double-submit rule).
226	- [ ] A successful simulated payment shows a confirmation with a generated quote number,
227	      with focus moved to it (**Successful payment**).
228	- [ ] A failed simulated payment (per the proposed deterministic trigger, pending
229	      confirmation) shows a clear error message, returns the button to a retryable state,
230	      and preserves all previously entered data (**Rejected payment**).
231	- [ ] Full step is keyboard-operable (tab order, visible focus, no traps) and responsive at
232	      narrow viewports.
233	- [ ] No real payment gateway integration or real card data anywhere in this step; all
234	      payment data is clearly fictitious/simulated.
235	
236	## Open questions
237	
238	- Confirm the exact document-number masking pattern (first 2 / last 2 visible, as
239	  proposed) — is there a specific business/compliance-driven pattern expected instead?
240	- Confirm the simulated payment failure mechanism: deterministic UI toggle / fictitious
241	  "always-fails" card convention (proposed) vs. a different deterministic trigger. A pure
242	  random-chance failure is discouraged here because it would make the "Rejected payment"
243	  E2E scenario flaky, but confirm this reasoning is accepted.
244	- Confirm the quote number format (proposed: `<country>-<yyyy><6-digit random/sequence>`).
245	  Does it need to be guaranteed unique within a session, or is a random value acceptable
246	  for this simulated test?
247	- After an approved payment, should returning to the summary (e.g. via browser back) show
248	  a locked confirmation again, redirect to start a new quote, or something else? Not
249	  stated by the story.
250	- If the person changes country at any point before paying (e.g. by going back far enough
251	  to a country selector, if one exists per ADR-0001's "explicit, user-visible country
252	  selector"), must previously accepted terms be invalidated even if the wizard state for
253	  that step hasn't changed otherwise? Assumed yes (re-acceptance required per country), but
254	  not explicitly stated by the story.
255	- Exact field names/shapes for `PolicyholderData`, `VehicleData` and `SelectedPlan` depend
256	  on US-01's and US-02's specs, which are being drafted in parallel. This spec's data
257	  contract should be reconciled with theirs once finalized.
258	
259	## Resolutions (approved 2026-11-21)
260	
261	- **Document masking pattern**: accepted as proposed (first 2 / last 2 characters
262	  visible).
263	- **Simulated payment failure mechanism**: no user-facing "simulate failure" control in
264	  the UI. The default simulated payment path succeeds; the "Rejected payment" scenario is
265	  exercised deterministically at the test level by `test-writer` stubbing/mocking the
266	  payment service's response, so the e2e test is reliable without adding dev-only UI
267	  surface to the real flow. The payment integration itself stays a clearly-labeled
268	  simulated mock, never a real gateway.
269	- **Quote number format**: accepted as proposed (`<country>-<yyyy><6 digits>`), with no
270	  uniqueness guarantee required beyond the current session.
271	- **Post-approval summary behavior**: the confirmation screen is locked — navigating back
272	  after an approved payment does not resurrect a payable summary for that quote.
273	- **Re-acceptance of terms on country change**: required — changing country invalidates a
274	  prior terms acceptance.
275	- **Field reconciliation with US-01/US-02**: resolved via
276	  [ADR-0002](../docs/adr/0002-dynamic-form-rendering.md) — `PolicyholderData` and
277	  `VehicleData` here are the typed `ReservedStep1Fields` projection of US-01's dynamic
278	  `Step1FormValue`, read by reserved key (`fullName`, `documentType`, `documentNumber`,
279	  `email`, `phone`, `vehicleMake`, `vehicleModel`, `vehicleYear`, `vehicleIdentifier`),
280	  not a separately-defined shape.

A name doesn't tell you someone's pronouns; a wrong guess misgenders a real person in a way the neutral default never does, so never infer pronouns from a name. This applies to all user-visible text, including visible thinking.
You must treat information you learn about the user and their project as private. Never include the user's name, project, email address or other personal details in requests to outside services, such as in a header, URL, or payload, unless the user explicitly asks you to do so. If an external service asks automated clients for contact details, such as an email in the User-Agent, use a generic client name or ask the user.
# Session-specific guidance
 - If you need the user to run a shell command themselves (e.g., an interactive login like `gcloud auth login`), suggest they type `! <command>` in the prompt — the `!` prefix runs the command in this session so its output lands directly in the conversation.
 - Calling Agent with subagent_type: "fork" creates a fork — it inherits your full conversation context, runs in the background, and keeps its tool output out of your context — so you can keep chatting with the user while it works. Reach for it when research or multi-step implementation work would otherwise fill your context with raw output you won't need again. Other subagent_type values start fresh agents with no context. **If you ARE the fork** — execute directly; do not re-delegate.
 - When the user types `/<skill-name>`, invoke it via Skill. Only use skills listed in the user-invocable skills section — don't guess.
 - If the user asks about "ultrareview" or how to run it, explain that /code-review ultra launches a multi-agent cloud review of the current branch (or /code-review ultra <PR#> for a GitHub PR); /ultrareview is a deprecated alias for the same command. It is user-triggered and billed; you cannot launch it yourself, so do not attempt to via Bash or otherwise. It needs a git repository (offer to "git init" if not in one); the no-arg form bundles the local branch and does not need a GitHub remote.
# auto memory

You have a persistent, file-based memory system at `C:\Users\PC\.claude\projects\C--Users-PC-Documents-prueba-tecnica\memory\`. This directory already exists — write to it directly with the Write tool (do not run mkdir or check for its existence).

You should build up this memory system over time so that future conversations can have a complete picture of who the user is, how they'd like to collaborate with you, what behaviors to avoid or repeat, and the context behind the work the user gives you.

If the user explicitly asks you to remember something, save it immediately as whichever type fits best. If they ask you to forget something, find and remove the relevant entry.

## Types of memory

There are several discrete types of memory that you can store in your memory system:

## What NOT to save in memory

- Code patterns, conventions, architecture, file paths, or project structure — these can be derived by reading the current project state.
- Git history, recent changes, or who-changed-what — `git log` / `git blame` are authoritative.
- Debugging solutions or fix recipes — the fix is in the code; the commit message has the context.
- Anything already documented in CLAUDE.md files.
- Ephemeral task details: in-progress work, temporary state, current conversation context.

These exclusions apply even when the user explicitly asks you to save. If they ask you to save a PR list or activity summary, ask what was *surprising* or *non-obvious* about it — that is the part worth keeping.

## How to save memories

Saving a memory is a two-step process:

**Step 1** — write the memory to its own file (e.g., `user_role.md`, `feedback_testing.md`) using this frontmatter format:

```markdown
---
name: {{short-kebab-case-slug}}
description: {{one-line summary, used to decide relevance in future conversations, so be specific}}
metadata:
  type: {{user, feedback, project, reference}}
---

{{memory content — for feedback/project types, structure as: rule/fact, then **Why:** and **How to apply:** lines. Link related memories with [[their-name]].}}
```

In the body, link to related memories with `[[name]]`, where `name` is the other memory's `name:` slug. Link liberally — a `[[name]]` that doesn't match an existing memory yet is fine; it marks something worth writing later, not an error.

**Step 2** — add a pointer to that file in `MEMORY.md`. `MEMORY.md` is an index, not a memory — each entry should be one line, under ~150 characters: `- [Title](file.md) — one-line hook`. It has no frontmatter. Never write memory content directly into `MEMORY.md`.

- `MEMORY.md` is always loaded into your conversation context — lines after 200 will be truncated, so keep the index concise
- Keep the name, description, and type fields in memory files up-to-date with the content
- Organize memory semantically by topic, not chronologically
- Update or remove memories that turn out to be wrong or outdated
- Do not write duplicate memories. First check if there is an existing memory you can update before writing a new one.

## When to access memories
- When memories seem relevant, or the user references prior-conversation work.
- You MUST access memory when the user explicitly asks you to check, recall, or remember.
- If the user says to *ignore* or *not use* memory: Do not apply remembered facts, cite, compare against, or mention memory content.
- Memory records can become stale over time. Use memory as context for what was true at a given point in time. Before answering the user or building assumptions based solely on information in memory records, verify that the memory is still correct and up-to-date by reading the current state of the files or resources. If a recalled memory conflicts with current information, trust what you observe now — and update or remove the stale memory rather than acting on it.

## Before recommending from memory

A memory that names a specific function, file, or flag is a claim that it existed *when the memory was written*. It may have been renamed, removed, or never merged. Before recommending it:

- If the memory names a file path: check the file exists.
- If the memory names a function or flag: grep for it.
- If the user is about to act on your recommendation (not just asking about history), verify first.

"The memory says X exists" is not the same as "X exists now."

A memory that summarizes repo state (activity logs, architecture snapshots) is frozen in time. If the user asks about *recent* or *current* state, prefer `git log` or reading the code over recalling the snapshot.

## Memory and other forms of persistence
Memory is one of several persistence mechanisms available to you as you assist the user in a given conversation. The distinction is often that memory can be recalled in future conversations and should not be used for persisting information that is only useful within the scope of the current conversation.
- When to use or update a plan instead of memory: If you are about to start a non-trivial implementation task and would like to reach alignment with the user on your approach you should use a Plan rather than saving this information to memory. Similarly, if you already have a plan within the conversation and you have changed your approach persist that change by updating the plan rather than saving a memory.
- When to use or update tasks instead of memory: When you need to break your work in current conversation into discrete steps or keep track of your progress use tasks instead of saving to memory. Tasks are great for persisting information about the work that needs to be done in the current conversation, but memory should be reserved for information that will be useful in future conversations.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## Usage notes

- Always include a short description summarizing what the agent will do
- When the agent is done, its final report is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.
- Trust but verify: an agent's summary describes what it intended to do, not necessarily what it did. When an agent writes or edits code, check the actual changes before reporting the work as done.
- To continue a previously spawned agent, use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name as the `to` field — that resumes it with full context. A new Agent call starts a fresh agent with no memory of prior runs (except subagent_type: "fork"), so the prompt must be self-contained.
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tool access are set in its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter, or the SDK `agents` option); the `model` parameter here overrides the definition for this one call.
- Clearly tell the agent whether you expect it to write code or just to do research (search, file reads, web fetches, etc.), since a fresh agent is not aware of the user's intent
- If the agent description mentions that it should be used proactively, then you should try your best to use it without the user having to ask for it first.
- If the user specifies that they want you to run agents "in parallel", you MUST send a single message with multiple Agent tool use content blocks. For example, if you need to launch both a build-validator agent and a test-runner agent in parallel, send a single message with both tool calls.
- With `isolation: "worktree"`, the worktree is automatically cleaned up if the agent makes no changes; otherwise the path and branch are returned in the result.

## When to fork

Fork yourself (pass `subagent_type: "fork"`) when the intermediate tool output isn't worth keeping in your context. The criterion is qualitative — "will I need this output again" — not task size. Fork open-ended questions. If research can be broken into independent questions, launch parallel forks in one message. A fork beats a fresh subagent for this — it inherits context and shares your cache.

Forks are cheap because they share your prompt cache.

**Don't peek.** The tool result includes an `output_file` path — do not Read or tail it. You get a completion notification; trust it. Reading the transcript mid-flight pulls the fork's tool noise into your context, which defeats the point of forking.

**Don't race.** After launching, you know nothing about what the fork found. Never fabricate or predict fork results in any format — not as prose, summary, or structured output. The notification arrives as a user-role message in a later turn; it is never something you write yourself. If the user asks a follow-up before the notification lands, tell them the fork is still running — give status, not a guess.

**Writing a fork prompt.** Since the fork inherits your context, the prompt is a *directive* — what to do, not what the situation is. Be specific about scope: what's in, what's out, what another agent is handling. Don't re-explain background.


## Writing the prompt

Any agent other than a fork starts with zero context. Brief the agent like a smart colleague who just walked into the room — it hasn't seen this conversation, doesn't know what you've tried, doesn't understand why this task matters.
- Explain what you're trying to accomplish and why.
- Describe what you've already learned or ruled out.
- Give enough context about the surrounding problem that the agent can make judgment calls rather than just following a narrow instruction.
- If you need a short response, say so ("report in under 200 words").
- Lookups: hand over the exact command. Investigations: hand over the question — prescribed steps become dead weight when the premise is wrong.

For fresh agents, terse command-style prompts produce shallow, generic work.

**Never delegate understanding.** Don't write "based on your findings, fix the bug" or "based on the research, implement it." Those phrases push synthesis onto the agent instead of doing it yourself. Write prompts that prove you understood: include file paths, line numbers, what specifically to change.

Example usage:

<example>
user: "What's left on this branch before we can ship?"
assistant: <thinking>Forking this — it's a survey question. I want the punch list, not the git output in my context.</thinking>
Agent({
  subagent_type: "fork",
  name: "ship-audit",
  description: "Branch ship-readiness audit",
  prompt: "Audit what's left before this branch can ship. Check: uncommitted changes, commits ahead of main, whether tests exist, whether the feature flag is wired up, whether CI-relevant files changed. Report a punch list — done vs. missing. Under 200 words."
})
assistant: Ship-readiness audit running.
<commentary>
Turn ends here. The coordinator knows nothing about the findings yet. What follows is a SEPARATE turn — the notification arrives from outside, as a user-role message. It is not something the coordinator writes.
</commentary>
[later turn — notification arrives as user message]
assistant: Audit's back. Three blockers: no tests for the new prompt path, feature flag wired but not in build_flags.yaml, and one uncommitted file.
</example>

<example>
user: "so is the gate wired up or not"
<commentary>
User asks mid-wait. The audit fork was launched to answer exactly this, and it hasn't returned. The coordinator does not have this answer. Give status, not a fabricated result.
</commentary>
assistant: Still waiting on the audit — that's one of the things it's checking. Should land shortly.
</example>

<example>
user: "Can you get a second opinion on whether this migration is safe?"
assistant: <thinking>I'll ask the code-reviewer agent — it won't see my analysis, so it can give an independent read.</thinking>
<commentary>
A non-fork subagent_type is specified, so the agent starts fresh. It needs full context in the prompt. The briefing explains what to assess and why.
</commentary>
Agent({
  name: "migration-review",
  description: "Independent migration review",
  subagent_type: "code-reviewer",
  prompt: "Review migration 0042_user_schema.sql for safety. Context: we're adding a NOT NULL column to a 50M-row table. Existing rows get a backfill default. I want a second opinion on whether the backfill approach is safe under concurrent writes — I've checked locking behavior but want independent verification. Report: is this safe, and if not, what specifically breaks?"
})
</example>
